Definition: from G4862 and G1011; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine:--consult, (give, take) counsel (together).
BiblicalUsage: The risen Christ counsels Laodicea to buy from Him gold tried in the fire and white raiment and eyesalve, and John notes that Caiaphas gave counsel to the Jews that it was expedient for one man to die for the people. One counsel saves and the other condemns, and the difference is whose voice you take it from.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Christ's counsel is the only advice worth buying at any price, because He counsels from love and Caiaphas counselled from fear.
